content.rendered:
Section 6 — Student Admission, Support & Progression

Section 6 — Student Admission, Support & Progression

Admission rules, intake statistics, fees, scholarships and student support systems.

Details of admission policy, statistics, fee structure and student support for academic year 2025–2026.
S.No. Item Details to be Provided
6.1 Admission Policy and Process Criteria: As per the Andhra Pradesh State Government admission policy.
Reservation policy: As per AP State Government rules.
Entrance exams:
  • AP EAPCET — for B.Tech
  • AP ICET — for MCA and MBA
  • APPGECET and GATE — for M.Tech
Detailed admission brochure and process links are available on the college website/admissions portal.
6.2 Year-wise Admission Statistics Academic Year: 2025–2026
Intake: B.Tech — 960; M.Tech — 144; MBA — 120; MCA — 60.
Applications / Admissions: 70% seats filled via State Govt counselling; Admitted: B.Tech — 977 (including 10% EWS quota), M.Tech — 115, MBA — 132 (including 10% EWS quota), MCA — 53.
Complete admission statistics (category-wise, gender-wise, region-wise) are available in annexure or institutional MIS.
6.3 Fee Structure Course-wise: Fees fixed as per AFRC.
Typical fees: B.Tech — Rs. 56,800/-; MBA & MCA — Rs. 35,000/-; M.Tech — Rs. 50,000/- (as notified).
Refund policy: Full refund of fee (minus processing fee up to Rs. 1,000) if a student withdraws before course commencement. If withdrawal happens after course start and the seat is filled, refund is pro-rated for the period occupied (minus deductions).
ANNEXURE – 6_3
Attach official fee notification, AFRC order and refund rules (annexure).
6.4 Scholarships and Financial Aid Institutional/Government/Endowment support: Provided as per State Government policy and institute-specific endowments.
Details of scholarship schemes, eligibility and application process can be found on the scholarships page or in annexures.
6.5 Student Demographics Gender, category and region distribution, nationality: Maintained as per State Government reservation rules and institutional records.
Downloadable demographic breakdown available from institutional MIS (category-wise, gender-wise, region-wise).
6.6 Mentoring and Counseling Academic & Personal Mentoring: Mentor-to-student ratio — 1 mentor per 20 students.
Details about mentoring assignments, counselling hours, and mental health resources are available with Student Affairs or Counselling Cell.
6.7 Student Grievance Redressal Link to Grievance Redressal Committee is available under Non-Statutory Committees on the website.
Online grievance filing mechanism and committee contact details provided on the institutional portal.
6.8 Anti-Ragging Measures Link to Anti-Ragging Committee available under Non-Statutory Committees on the website; ragging prevention measures and helpline numbers are displayed across campus.
Anti-ragging affidavits and monitoring committee details are maintained as per UGC/AICTE rules.
6.9 Alumni Network Link to Alumni Committee available under Non-Statutory Committees; alumni engagement, placement support and mentoring initiatives are coordinated via Alumni Office.

Admission:
  • 70% of students admitted through EAPCET counselling conducted by State Government.

Ethics:
  • Use knowledge and skill for enhancement of human welfare.
  • Be honest and impartial and serve with fidelity their clients (including employers) and the public.

2.6 Strategic / Institutional Development Plan Short-term Goals:
  1. Practice total quality management to ensure student-centered teaching-learning processes.
  2. Ensure academic excellence with high pass rates in university examinations.
  3. Arrange placements by developing personality and technical skills.
  4. Conduct programs on personality development, entrepreneurship, and co-/extra-curricular activities.
  5. Enhance MOUs with industries for placements, projects and training.
  6. Undertake consultancy and sponsored research with external organizations.

M.Tech Programs at St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology

At St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, we offer a range of advanced postgraduate programs designed to empower the next generation of engineers and technologists. Our M.Tech courses provide in-depth knowledge, hands-on experience, and research opportunities in cutting-edge fields, tailored to meet industry demands and technological advancements.

Specializations Offered

  • Embedded Systems (Year of Start – 2013)
    Dive into the world of microcontrollers, IoT devices, real-time systems, and hardware-software integration. Our Embedded Systems specialization equips students with the skills needed to design and develop intelligent embedded solutions for various industries.

  • Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI & ML) (Year of Start – 2025)
    Explore advanced concepts in AI, deep learning, data mining, and predictive analytics. This specialization prepares students to innovate and solve complex problems using intelligent algorithms and data-driven techniques.

  • Computer Science and Engineering (Year of Start – 2007)
    Gain expertise in software development, data structures, algorithms, and emerging technologies such as cloud computing, cybersecurity, and big data. This program fosters strong problem-solving and research skills in core computer science.

  • Power Systems (Year of Start – 2013)
    Focus on the analysis, design, and management of electrical power generation, transmission, and distribution systems. This specialization prepares students for challenges in renewable energy, smart grids, and sustainable power solutions.

  • Transportation Engineering (Year of start – 2015)
    Learn the principles of planning, design, operation, and maintenance of transportation systems. This program emphasizes sustainable and efficient transport infrastructure development.

  • Thermal Engineering (Year of Start – 2014)
    Study the fundamentals and applications of thermodynamics, heat transfer, and energy systems. This specialization is ideal for those aiming to excel in energy management, HVAC systems, and thermal power plants.

Intake Capacity

Each specialization admits 24 students per academic year, ensuring a focused and interactive learning environment.

Internal Complaints Committee

Preamble of the Internal Complaints Committee

The Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) is established to promote a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment within our institution. Recognizing the right of every individual to work and study in an atmosphere free from harassment and discrimination, the ICC is committed to addressing grievances related to sexual harassment and any form of misconduct.

The committee aims to create awareness about the issues of harassment and to provide a platform for individuals to voice their concerns without fear of retaliation. Through transparent procedures and fair investigations, the ICC will ensure that complaints are handled promptly and sensitively.

We believe that fostering a culture of respect, dignity, and equality is paramount to the well-being of our community. The ICC is dedicated to implementing preventive measures, conducting educational programs, and promoting a zero-tolerance policy towards any form of harassment. By encouraging open dialogue and supporting affected individuals, we strive to maintain a safe and supportive environment for all.

Roles, Responsibilities and Statutes

SACET is a coeducational institution providing equal opportunities to all and is working towards providing a congenial atmosphere for men and women to work together. SACET has formed an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), as mandated by the regulatory authorities and POSH Act, to address and initiate appropriate action on complaints involving physical contacts or advances, demand for sexual favours, sexually tainted remarks, and any unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal expressions of a sexual nature.

Any aggrieved person (employee, visitor or student) who has suffered harassment at the workplace can approach the ICC. This committee aims at sensitizing the students and staff to work diligently to prevent sexual harassment in the college and work towards the redressal of sexual harassment cases.

The functions of ICC shall be to:

  1. Prevent sexual harassment at the workplace.
  2. Prevent discrimination and sexual harassment against girls by promoting gender amity among students and employees.
  3. Conduct periodical programmes on women empowerment.
  4. Provide a conducive environment and congenial atmosphere for women.

In case of any complaint, kindly register through email:

A Six Day FDP on POWER CONVERTERS AND CONTROL TECHNIQUES FOR MICROGRIDS AND ELECTRIC VEHICLES

  • Proposed Title & Objective
  • About The Institute
  • About the Department
  • Topics Covered Under FDP

Proposed Title:

Power Converters and Control Techniques for Microgrids and Electric vehicles

Objective:

The proposed FDP on “Power Converters and Control Techniques for Microgrids and Electric vehicles

”isaspecializedprogramthatfocuses on state of art technologies related to converter design and control for microgrid and electrical vehicles. This FDPtargets the research scholars working in the respective domains, to clarify their doubts in their relevant working research topics. This also helps the faculty to update their knowledge in the respective domains to give better understanding in the topics in the newly introduced courses. It helps the students to meet the current industry requirement. It also supports start-up entrepreneurs in the respective areas.

St. Ann's College of Engineering & Technology (SACET) was established in the year2001 at Vetapalem Mandal, Chirala, Prakasam District, Andhra Pradesh bythe St. MaryEducational Society, pioneered by Educationalists, Industrialists and Philanthropists. TheCollege is housed amidst lush green fields, in serene environment, free from pollution andconductiveforthepursuitofeducation.
TheInstitutionisApprovedbyAICTE,NewDelhiandseveral departments of the Institute are Accredited by National Board of Accreditation(NBA) multiple times and also the Institution has permanent membership in Institution ofEngineers(I).TheinstituteisAutonomous fromtheacademicyear2023-24onwards. The Institution is Accredited by NAAC with ‘A’ Grade in I, II and III cycles.Recognized by UGC Under Section 2(f) and 12(B) of UGC Act, 1956 and also Awarded ‘A’GradebyAndhraPradeshStateGovernment.ThecollegehasMOUwithISROSpaceApplication Center, Ahmadabad and received 3 IRNSS receiver kits for GPS data collection.The college is approved as TSDI [SEIMENS] by AP State Government. The institution hasorganizedvarious governmentfunded andInstitutionfundedFDPsandWorkshops.

About the Department:

From a modest beginning in 2001, the Electrical and Electronics Engineering Department in St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology (SACET), Chirala has now grown into a fully integrated department in the field of Engineering and Technology. It is an “education with future”. Learning how to inquire, converse and collaborate, the skill that never go out of date. The objectives of imparting education, combined with creation, dissemination and application of knowledge are being met in an integrated form to create a synergetic impact.

To fulfill its mission in new and powerful ways, faculty, staff and student of the department strives to achieve excellence in every endeavour – be it education, research, consulting or training-by making continuous improvements in curricula and pedagogical tools. The faculty of the department published research papers in various reputed international journals and conferences with good number of papers published in SCOPUS/SCI indexed journals. The department of EEE has surpassed many milestones under the able and dynamic leadership of its HOD Dr. SVD Anil Kumar. Some of the notable achievements are: UG NBA accreditation – 2009-2016 NAAC Accreditation 2011 and 2016 Controller of Examinations – 2006 to till date

  1. Overview of power converters for renewable energy systems.
  2. Mathematical Modelling and Simulation of Microgrid
  3. FPGA implementation in Power electronic converters
  4. DG penetration and Power Quality assessment and mitigation in Distribution Network
  5. Design switched-mode power converters for RE and EV systems.
  6. Impact of EV charging station on distribution system
  7. Electric Vehicle chargers design and optimization techniques
  8. Real time and Virtual simulations on EV, BMS and Microgrid Applications
  9. V2G &G2V systems & issues.
  10. Reliability Aspects of Power Electronics Converters
  11. Model based development for EV applications in MATLAB

Coordinator

The Co-ordinatorpublished more than 35 Research papers in international journals and conferences. His research interests are mainly focused on Harmonic analysis in power systems. He also has rich experience in organizing various funded FDPs and workshops.

About Forum
Music & Fine Arts club involves every student of the college, irrespective of the department they belong to. Cultural Club help students keep in touch with the rich cultural values, customs and traditions of our country. Extracurricular activities increase opportunities for social interaction and new relationship development. As most of these activities are group-oriented which have students from different niches, which gives them a chance to more know about people of different passions and cultures. Besides, this they can also find clubs or groups that share similar social, religious or even entertainment interest for socialization. Interaction with people of different backgrounds helps in development of interpersonal skills of students.

 

Forum Objectives

  1. To mould the personality of students and exposes them to a wide range of cultural events throughout the year.
  2. To participate in a multitude of events, the students also get a first hand experience of organizing and managing the events it caters to the creative needs of the students.
  3. To give a platform to creativity, the Club also aims at developing the intellectual, organizational and social skills of the students.
  4. To develope students skills like leadership, working in a team, sharing success and failure, accepting responsibility are implicit in the working of the club.

ALL ABOUT CIVIL

The department of Civil Engineering was established in the year 2011 with an intake of 60. Eight batches of students nearly 480 have successfully completed their graduation so far from the department. Our strength is our faculty. We have twelve dedicated faculty members and three supporting staff members. In 2015 the department has also started Master of Technology (M. Tech) programme with initial intake of 24 students with Transportation Engineering as specialization.

The department has nine physical laboratories to fulfill the needs of academic and industrial requirements including are Concrete, Transportation Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering , Environmental Engineering , Survey , Geology , Hydraulic Engineering , Computer aided engineering , GIS & CAD lab, Strength of materials, FM & HM Lab and Irrigation Design and Drawing. All laboratories are equipped with state of the art equipment to suit the emerging technologies and career opportunities

The students are prepared with multi-dimensional skill sets covering all the required graduate attributes. More focus is given on practical learning, projects, and research. The department is plans guest lecturers from industry personnel, industrial visits and tours every year to fill the gap between academia and industry. The department is also conducting workshops and conferences at regular intervals in the latest and innovative areas of civil engineering.

The board of studies of civil engineering is constituted by taking the services emerging technologies career of students. Many students are qualified in Gate Exam, got placements in civil engineering core companies, Sachivalayam jobs as well. With software career options open for aspiring civil engineering students so far 50 students were placed in companies like Infosys, TCS, Wipro, Capgemini, Amazon, Virtusa, Sutherland  etc.

 

VISION

To become a nationally recognized centre for Civil Engineering Education with effective Teaching and Learning practices

MISSION

DM1: To produce competent Civil Engineering students with ability to design, develop and problem solving skills.

DM2:  To produce students with ability to use modern tools along with life long learning skills..

DM3: To promote entrepreneurship and soft skills.

DM4: To promote industry interaction, consultancy and concern for the society.

ALL ABOUT THE COLLEGE

St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology – AUTONOMOUS (Non-Minority College) was established in the year 2001 at Vetapalem Mandal, Chirala, Bapatla District, Andhra Pradesh by The St. Mary Educational Society, pioneered by Educationalists, Industrialists and Philanthropists. The College is housed amidst lush green fields, in serene environment, free from pollution and conductive for the pursuit of education. Bay of Bengal is just two km away from the college.

The Institution is Approved by All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), New Delhi and is Permanently Affiliated to the Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Kakinada.Five Programmes were Accredited by National Board of Accredition(NBA).The Institution is Accredited by NAAC with ‘A’ Grade.The Institution is recognized by UGC under section 2(f) and 12(B).The Institution is awarded ‘A’ grade by Andhra Pradesh State Government. The Institution is Permanently Accredited by Institution of Engineers(I).Institution is selected for Andhra Pradesh State Technical Skill Development Center(Siemens).The College has a glory of experience in teaching from 2001 onwards. The College is situated along the Bypass Road at 6 KMs distance Chirala town in Chirala-Ongole stretch. The College campus has a sprawling area of around 24.3 1/2 acres, with serene atmosphere, sylvan settings and environs, conductive for academic activities. The college is well connected by rail and road links because of its ideal location.

 

VISION

To develop St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology – AUTONOMOUS into an Institution of Global standards catering to the educational needs of students and also contribute to the welfare of local Community.

MISSION

To impart total quality education at Under Graduate and Post Graduate levels by: Inculcating best teaching and learning practices; providing opportunities for faculty development, Consultancy, Research; striving for maximum results in the examinations; Creating avenues for industry interaction to provide training and placement opportunities; managing the institution with good governance and transparency and strive for well-being of local community.

ALL ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT

AI and Machine Learning jobs have jumped by almost 75 percent over the past four years and are poised to keep growing. Similar to data analysts, statisticians, and business analysts, AI is one of the fastest growing, in-demand fields and lucrative career choices. A study by Oxford University and Yale University indicates that AI will outperform humans in many ways and will automate all human jobs in the next 120 years. By 2024, AI will be better than humans at translation, will write bestselling books by 2049, and will perform surgeries by 2053.

                              The global conversational AI market size was valued at USD 5.78 billion in 2020 and is projected to reach USD 32.62 billion by 2030, registering a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 20.0% from 2021 to 2030. The field of artificial intelligence has a tremendous career outlook, with the Bureau of Labor Statistics predicting a 31.4 percent, by 2030, increase in jobs for data scientists and mathematical science professionals, which are crucial to AI. In their global AI study, PwC estimates that by 2030, the global GDP will have increased by 26 percent due to AI alone. That’s more than the current GDP of China and India combined. PwC isn’t the only optimist in the room. The World Economic Forum estimates that 97 million new jobs will be created through AI by 2025. With a humongous amount of data becoming more available today, Machine Learning is starting to move to the cloud. Data Scientists will no longer explicitly custom code or manage infrastructure. A.I. and ML will help the systems to scale for them, generate new models on the go and deliver faster and accurate results.

Pursuing a machine learning job is a solid choice for a high-paying career that will be in demand for decades. AIML provides applications that have an ability to learn through the experience without being explicitly programmed.

Machine Learniing enables applications to recognize patterns in the data in the same way as human brains do. It has become an integral part of our day to day lives and few of the widely used applications are Traffic Alerts, Social Media (Facebook, Twitter), Product Recommendations (Amazon, FlipKart), Virtual Personal Assistants (Siri, Google Assist), Directions in Google maps, Self-Driving Cars, Online Video Streaming (NetFlix). About IQAC

National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) proposes that every accredited institution should establish an Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) as a post-accreditation quality sustenance measure for its action plan for performance evaluation, assessment & accreditation and quality up-gradation of institutions of higher education. Since quality enhancement is a continuous process, the IQAC will become a part of the institution’s system & work towards realization of the goals of quality enhancement & sustenance. The prime task of the IQAC is to develop a system for conscious, consistent & catalytic improvement in the overall performance of institutions. IQAC was established in SACET on 17-04-2012. It has been channelizing all efforts & measures of the institution towards promoting its holistic academic excellence. IQAC will facilitate to ensure heightened level of clarity and focus in institutional functioning towards quality enhancement, ensure internalization of the quality culture, ensure enhancement and coordination among various activities of the institution and institutionalize all good practices, provide a sound basis for decision-making to improve institutional functioning, act as a dynamic system for quality changes in HEIs, build an organized methodology of documentation and internal communication.

VISION

To develop St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology into an Institution of Global standards catering to the educational needs of students and also contribute to the welfare of local Community.

MISSION

To impart total quality education at Under Graduate and Post Graduate levels by Inculcating best teaching and learning practices providing opportunities for faculty development, Consultancy, Research; striving for maximum results in the examinations. Creating avenues for industry interaction to provide training and placement opportunities managing the institution with good governance and transparency and strive for well-being of local community.

    5. The credibility of assessment and evaluation process

    7. Sharing of research findings and networking with other institutions in India and abroad.

FUNCTIONS

    required knowledge and technology for participatory teaching and learning process

Internet of Things (IoT)

 

Connecting the Physical World with Digital Intelligence

Introduction to IoT

The Internet of Things (IoT) refers to the rapidly growing network of physical devices,
machines, vehicles, appliances, sensors and other objects that are connected to the Internet and capable
of collecting, processing and exchanging data.

These connected devices use sensors, software, communication technologies and computing systems to gather
information from their surroundings. The collected information can then be transmitted through wired or
wireless networks to other devices, applications or cloud platforms for processing and analysis.

With the availability of low-cost computer chips, sensors, cloud computing and high-speed wireless networks,
almost any physical object can become part of an IoT ecosystem. From smart watches and home appliances to
industrial machines, automobiles, agricultural equipment and aircraft, IoT is creating a connected environment
where physical objects can communicate and exchange information with minimal human intervention.

What Makes IoT Different?

Traditional devices generally perform a specific function without being able to understand or communicate
information about their surroundings. IoT adds a layer of digital intelligence by connecting these devices
to networks and equipping them with sensors and software.

For example, a traditional temperature sensor may simply display the temperature. An IoT-enabled temperature
sensor can continuously measure the temperature, send the information to a cloud platform, analyze the data
and automatically trigger an action when a particular threshold is reached.

Key Components of IoT

Sensors & Devices

Sensors collect information from the physical environment such as temperature, humidity, pressure,
motion, location, light, sound and vibration.

Connectivity

IoT devices communicate using technologies such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular networks, Zigbee, RFID,
LoRaWAN and other communication protocols.

Data Processing

Collected data is processed using edge computing, cloud platforms and specialized software to identify
patterns and generate useful information.

Applications & Users

Applications transform processed data into meaningful insights, dashboards, alerts, recommendations and
automated actions.

How Does IoT Work?

An IoT system generally follows a continuous cycle of sensing, communication, processing, analysis and action.
The process can be summarized as follows:

01

Sense

Sensors collect information from the environment.

02

Connect

The device transmits data through a network.

03

Process

Data is processed locally or in the cloud.

04

Analyze

Software analyzes the collected information.

05

Act

The system generates an alert or performs an action.

Applications of IoT

Smart Homes

IoT enables smart lighting, smart thermostats, security cameras, door locks, appliances and energy
management systems that can be monitored and controlled remotely.

Healthcare

Connected medical devices and wearable technologies can collect and transmit health-related measurements,
support remote monitoring and help healthcare professionals make informed decisions.

Smart Agriculture

IoT sensors can monitor soil moisture, temperature, weather conditions and crop environments, helping
farmers improve irrigation, resource utilization and agricultural productivity.

Industrial IoT

Factories use connected machines and sensors to monitor equipment performance, detect abnormalities,
optimize production and support predictive maintenance.

Smart Cities

IoT technologies can support intelligent traffic management, smart parking, waste management, public
lighting, environmental monitoring and energy management.

Connected Vehicles

Modern vehicles can use IoT technologies for location tracking, vehicle diagnostics, navigation,
safety systems, fleet management and communication with other systems.

Benefits of IoT

  • Automation: IoT systems can automate repetitive tasks and processes.
  • Real-Time Monitoring: Devices can provide continuous information about equipment,
    environments and operations.
  • Improved Efficiency: Data-driven systems can help organizations use energy, materials,
    time and other resources more efficiently.
  • Predictive Maintenance: Sensors can identify unusual patterns and potential equipment
    failures before they become serious problems.
  • Better Decision Making: Real-time data and analytics can support faster and more informed decisions.
  • Enhanced User Experience: Connected products can provide personalized, responsive and
    convenient services.

IoT, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence

IoT devices can generate enormous amounts of data because they continuously collect information from the
physical world. This data becomes especially valuable when combined with Big Data analytics
and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

AI and machine learning algorithms can analyze IoT data to identify patterns, predict future events and
support automated decision-making. This combination is helping organizations move from simple monitoring
systems toward intelligent and autonomous systems.

Challenges of IoT

Security

Large numbers of connected devices increase the potential attack surface and require strong security measures.

Privacy

Connected devices may collect sensitive or personal information, making responsible data management important.

Interoperability

Different manufacturers and platforms may use different technologies and communication standards.

Data Management

The enormous volume of information generated by IoT devices requires scalable storage, processing and
analytics infrastructure.

Future of IoT

The future of IoT is closely connected with developments in artificial intelligence, edge computing,
advanced sensors, cloud computing, robotics and next-generation wireless networks. As these technologies
continue to evolve, IoT systems are expected to become more intelligent, efficient and autonomous.

The integration of IoT with AI and machine learning will enable systems to understand their environments,
predict events and take appropriate actions with limited human intervention. This can create new
opportunities across healthcare, manufacturing, transportation, agriculture, education, energy and
smart-city development.

Conclusion

The Internet of Things is transforming ordinary physical objects into connected and intelligent systems.
By combining sensors, connectivity, computing and data analytics, IoT enables devices to collect information,
communicate with one another and respond to changing conditions.

From smart homes and healthcare to agriculture, manufacturing and smart cities, IoT is becoming an important
part of modern digital transformation. As connectivity and intelligent technologies continue to advance,
IoT will play an increasingly important role in creating a more connected, efficient and responsive world.

Program Educational Objectives, Outcomes & PSOs

CSE – Internet of Things

Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)

CSE–IoT graduates are expected to achieve the following objectives.

PEO1

Engineering Knowledge & IoT Solutions

Graduates apply knowledge of computing, electronics, embedded systems and IoT to design effective engineering solutions.

PEO2

Professional Careers

Graduates build successful careers in IoT, computing and related engineering domains.

PEO3

Higher Education, Research & Innovation

Graduates pursue higher education, research, innovation or entrepreneurship with a commitment to lifelong learning.

PEO4

Professionalism, Ethics & Sustainable Solutions

Graduates demonstrate professionalism, teamwork, ethics, collaboration with industry and research bodies to develop sustainable IoT-based solutions for societal needs.

Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs)

CSE–IoT graduates will be able to:

PSO1

IoT Design, Development & Deployment

Acquire knowledge on the design, development and deployment of CSE and IoT based solutions using sensors, microcontrollers, embedded systems, network protocols, cloud services and analytics tools.

PSO2

Industry-Oriented Projects

Apply cutting-edge techniques and tools to develop CSE-IoT based projects individually or in teamwork to address industrial challenges.

PSO3

IoT Data Analytics & Security

Analyse IoT data using machine learning techniques and apply security principles to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and resilience of IoT systems.

Program Outcomes (POs)

Engineering graduates are expected to demonstrate the following outcomes.

PO1

Engineering Knowledge

Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop to the solution of complex engineering problems.

WK1 – WK4
PO2

Problem Analysis

Identify, formulate, review research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions with consideration for sustainable development. (WK1 to WK4)

WK1 – WK4
PO3

Design/Development of Solutions

Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design/develop systems/components/ processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, culture, society and environment as required. (WK5)

WK5
PO4

Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems

Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modelling, analysis & interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8).

WK8
PO5

Engineering Tool Usage

Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering & IT tools, including prediction and modelling recognizing their limitations to solve complex engineering problems. (WK2 and WK6)

WK2 & WK6
PO6

The Engineer and The World

Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7).

WK1, WK5 & WK7
PO7

Ethics

Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclusion; adhere to national & international laws. (WK9)

WK9
PO8

Individual and Collaborative Team Work

Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse/multi-disciplinary teams.

PO9

Communication

Communicate effectively and inclusively within the engineering community and society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences.

PO10

Project Management and Finance

Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

PO11

Life-Long Learning

Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change. (WK8)

WK8

Knowledge and Attitude Profile – WK1 to WK9

WK1

Natural Sciences & Social Sciences

Systematic, theory-based understanding of natural sciences applicable to the discipline, with awareness of relevant social sciences.

WK2

Mathematics, Data Analysis & Computing

Conceptually based mathematics, numerical analysis, data analysis, statistics, and formal aspects of computer/information science supporting analysis and modelling.

WK3

Engineering Fundamentals

Systematic, theory-based formulation of engineering fundamentals required in the engineering discipline.

WK4

Engineering Specialist Knowledge

Engineering specialist knowledge providing theoretical frameworks and bodies of knowledge for accepted practice areas; including knowledge at the forefront of the discipline.

WK5

Engineering Design & Operations

Knowledge supporting engineering design and operations, including efficient resource use, environmental impacts, whole-life cost, reuse of resources, net-zero carbon and related concepts.

WK6

Engineering Practice & Technology

Knowledge of engineering practice and technology in the practice areas of the engineering discipline.

WK7

Engineering, Society & Sustainability

Knowledge of the role of engineering in society and identified issues in engineering practice, including professional responsibility, public safety and sustainable development.

WK8

Research, Critical Thinking & Creativity

Engagement with current research literature, critical thinking and creative approaches for evaluating emerging issues in the discipline.

WK9

Ethics & Professional Conduct

Ethics, inclusive behaviour and professional conduct, including professional responsibilities, engineering norms, diversity, mutual understanding and respect.

ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT

The Internet of Things, or IoT, refers to the billions of physical devices around the world that are now connected to the internet, all collecting and sharing data. Thanks to the arrival of super-cheap computer chips and the ubiquity of wireless networks, it’s possible to turn anything, from something as small as a pill to something as big as an aeroplane, into a part of the IoT. Connecting up all these different objects and adding sensors to them adds a level of digital intelligence to devices that would be otherwise dumb, enabling them to communicate real-time data without involving a human being. The Internet of Things is making the fabric of the world around us more smarter and more responsive, merging the digital and physical universes.

JOIN US

ABOUT HEAD OF THE DEPARTMENT

Dr Indraneel  is a Ratified Professor from JNTUK and guiding 4 Ph.D Scholars from ANNAMALAI UNIVERSITY,  Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu as external supervisor. 

He is a peer reviewer and editorial board member for various journals like Elsevier, i-manager’s JCOM journalas etc. 

He got appreciation from APSSSDC for best services as SPOC-APPSSDC-SIEMENS-TSDI Centre in SACET in 2017

KNOW MORE

VISION

To develop the CSE–IoT department into a centre of excellence in computing and Internet of Things by imparting quality education, fostering innovation and providing industry-aligned skills that empower students to contribute to technological advancement and the welfare of society.

MISSION

The CSE–IoT department strives:

M1: To provide strong foundations in computing, IoT technologies and interdisciplinary problem solving through effective teaching–learning practices.
M2: To promote research, innovation and continuous professional development of faculty and students.
M3: To enhance employability through industry collaborations, internships, training and placement support in emerging IoT and related domains.
M4: To inculcate ethical values, social responsibility and commitment to community welfare through technology-enabled solutions.
M5: To ensure transparent and student-centric academic processes aligned with global standards in engineering education.

PEO3: Graduates pursue higher education, research, innovation or entrepreneurship with a commitment to lifelong learning.

PEO4: Graduates demonstrate professionalism, teamwork, ethics, collaboration with industry and research bodies to develop sustainable IoT-based solutions for societal needs.

PO11: Project management and finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and

Career Outlook

Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning

 

A Fast-Growing Career Domain

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have emerged as some of the most
transformative technologies of the 21st century. Organizations across industries are increasingly
adopting intelligent systems to automate processes, analyze large volumes of data, improve
decision-making, personalize customer experiences, and develop innovative products and services.

As a result, demand for professionals with expertise in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning,
Data Science, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, and related technologies
continues to increase. For students with strong foundations in mathematics, programming, statistics,
and problem-solving, AI & ML offers a wide range of exciting and rewarding career opportunities.

75%
Growth in AI & Machine Learning jobs over the referenced four-year period

HIGH DEMAND
AI is among the fastest-growing technology and career domains

GLOBAL
AI skills are relevant across industries and geographical markets

Why Choose AI & Machine Learning?

 

Industry Demand


AI expertise is increasingly required in technology, finance, healthcare, manufacturing,
education, retail, transportation, cybersecurity, and many other sectors.

Lucrative Careers


Professionals with specialized AI and ML skills can pursue technically challenging and
financially rewarding careers.

Innovation


AI enables the development of intelligent products, automated systems, predictive models,
recommendation engines, and advanced digital solutions.

Career Opportunities in AI & ML

 


AI Engineer

Designs and develops intelligent software systems and AI-powered applications.


Machine Learning Engineer

Builds, trains, evaluates, and deploys machine learning models.


Data Scientist

Extracts insights from complex datasets using statistics, programming, and machine learning.


Deep Learning Engineer

Develops neural-network-based solutions for complex AI applications.


NLP Engineer

Develops systems capable of understanding and processing human language.


Computer Vision Engineer

Creates AI systems that interpret and analyze images, video, and visual information.


AI Researcher

Conducts research to develop new algorithms, models, and intelligent computing techniques.


AI Product Specialist

Combines technology and business knowledge to develop AI-enabled products and services.

The Future of Artificial Intelligence

Research into the future impact of Artificial Intelligence has highlighted the possibility that
increasingly capable AI systems could outperform humans in a growing number of specialized tasks.
Forecasts have suggested that AI could significantly transform areas such as translation, content
creation, scientific research, healthcare, and surgery.

Earlier forecasts associated with research from Oxford and Yale University proposed specific
milestones for AI capabilities, including advances in translation, writing, and surgical procedures.
Such forecasts should be viewed as projections rather than guaranteed dates, because the pace and
direction of AI development depend on technological, economic, regulatory, and societal factors.


Future Outlook

AI is expected to continue reshaping the nature of work rather than simply eliminating every job.
Many occupations are likely to change as AI automates routine activities while increasing the value
of human capabilities such as creativity, critical thinking, leadership, communication, domain
expertise, and ethical judgment. Students who develop strong technical foundations and continuously
update their AI skills can position themselves well for this evolving employment landscape.

About HOD

Dr. Hari Kishan Chapala

Dr. Hari Kishan Chapala has received Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering in 2013 from Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh.

He is working as Professor and Head in the Department of CSE – AI & ML, St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala.

He has a total of 26 years of experience in Teaching and Administration. He is ratified by JNTUK, Kakinada in 2016.

He has authored and published more than 25 research papers in reputed journals and presented papers in 8 International Conferences.

He has 12 patent publications and has secured four Best Teacher Awards in recognition of his contribution to teaching and education.

He is nominated as Q-Leader by APSCHE.

VISION

 

To build the Department of Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning into a
Centre of Excellence that nurtures globally competent professionals,
advances innovative research, and delivers AI-driven solutions for societal and local community development.

MISSION

 

1

To impart quality education in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning through innovative
teaching-learning processes and a curriculum aligned with global standards.

2

industry-institute interaction in emerging areas of Artificial Intelligence.

PEOs, PSOs, POs

Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)

PEO 1

To empower graduates to apply fundamental engineering concepts and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning principles to analyze, design, and implement effective solutions for complex real-world problems.

PEO 2

To prepare graduates with advanced technical skills and professional competence to excel in careers and innovative projects in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.

PEO 3

To nurture graduates with an entrepreneurial mindset, ethical awareness, teamwork and communication skills, and lifelong learning abilities to contribute effectively to society and national economic development.

Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs)

PSO 1

Apply core principles of computer science and engineering to design, develop, and evaluate intelligent computing systems using Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Data Analytics for real-world applications.

PSO 2

Analyze and process structured and unstructured data to build, optimize, and deploy end-to-end AI&ML solutions using modern tools, frameworks, cloud platforms, and engineering practices.

PSO 3

Apply ethical, transparent, secure, and socially responsible practices in the development, deployment, and use of AI and ML technologies.

Program Outcomes (POs)

Graduates of the programme are expected to attain the following Program Outcomes.

PO1: Engineering Knowledge

Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop to the solution of complex engineering problems.

WK1 – WK4

PO2: Problem Analysis

Identify, formulate, review research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions with consideration for sustainable development. (WK1 to WK4)

WK1 – WK4

PO3: Design/Development of Solutions

Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design/develop systems/components/ processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, culture, society and environment as required. (WK5)

WK5

PO4: Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems

Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modelling, analysis & interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8).

WK8

PO5: Engineering Tool Usage

Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering & IT tools, including prediction and modelling recognizing their limitations to solve complex engineering problems. (WK2 and WK6)

WK2 & WK6

PO6: The Engineer and The World

Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7).

WK1, WK5 & WK7

PO7: Ethics

Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclusion; adhere to national & international laws. (WK9)

WK9

PO8: Individual and Collaborative Team Work

Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse/multi-disciplinary teams.

TEAM WORK

PO9: Communication

Communicate effectively and inclusively within the engineering community and society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences.

COMMUNICATION

PO10: Project Management and Finance

Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

MANAGEMENT & FINANCE

PO11: Life-Long Learning

Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change. (WK8)

Research, Critical Thinking & Creativity

WK9

Ethics & Professional Conduct

Ethics, inclusive behaviour and professional conduct, including professional responsibilities, engineering norms, diversity, mutual understanding and respect.

Society Number : 16 of 2009

St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology is all set to have an Alumni association.

SACET ALUMNI MOTTO
“To go forth with values that we have learned at SACET and share them with family and the community at large”.

“Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much.”

St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology will offer a wide range of resources for alumni, including Refresher Courses, Post Graduate Information, Higher Educational Opportunities in India or Abroad.

 

Some of the main objectives of the alumni association will be :-

  • To enhance the interaction between the past and present students.

  • To enhance and modernize the existing facilities of the college.

  • To provide industrial training, placements and other facilities to the students with the assistance of the past students.

  • To circulate books to the students who are in need.

  • To promote cultural, sports and other extracurricular activities.

  • To Provide monetary assistance to the deserving students

Alumni are the strength of the St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology. SACET takes great pride in the Alumni as the members are all in highly respectable professional positions in various industries and are closely associated with the college. Every Year College organizes an Alumni meeting to provide a platform for the seniors to give suggestions and experiences to the juniors on career, industry opportunities, higher education (India / Overseas), Feedback / Suggestions for improvement on training etc.

ADMISSION PROCEDURE

Regular Admission Procedure:

A Candidate for admission to the four-year degree course in Engineering must have passed the Intermediate examination of the Board of Intermediate Education, Government of Andhra Pradesh or any other examination as equivalent there to.

The admission to the B.Tech. course, excepting NRI Quota, is through a State-Level Entrance Test called “Engineering, Agriculture and Pharmacy Common Entrance Test” (APEAPCET), conducted by the Government of Andhra Pradesh. All eligible applicants have to qualify in the entrance test, EAPCET. The candidates will be admitted strictly in accordance with the merit secured in the EAPCET. The Convener-AC of APEAPCET admits the candidates based on marks secured in Intermediate or an equivalent examination and the rank secured in APEAPCET.

College Counselling Code: ANSN

Management Quota Admission Procedure:

The Management admits candidates for the Management and NRI quota based on merit. The candidates should have a first class in Intermediate or qualifying examination or 50% secured in optional subjects: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry.

The Convener of ECET admits the candidates from the stream of Diploma Holders to II Year B.Tech.

The qualification needed is a pass in Diploma in relevant branch and also qualified in ECET examination conducted by the State Government as per the G.O. Ms. No. 61 Dated 26-05-2006. Regular Admission – Polytechnic Diploma – Eligibility Requirements Selection of candidates is governed by the Rules and regulations laid down in this regard from time to time.

Candidates who wish to seek admission in any of the Diploma courses will have to appear for Common Entrance Examination, Andhra Pradesh Polytechnic Common Entrance Test (AP POLYCET) conducted by the State Board of Technical Education and Training (SBTET), Andhra Pradesh. Only the candidates satisfying the following requirements will be eligible to appear for AP POLYCET.

1. The candidates seeking admission should have appeared for the X Class examination, conducted by the Board of Secondary Education, Andhra Pradesh or equivalent Examination thereto, at the time of making application to the Common Entrance Examination for Polytechnics (AP POLYCET). In case candidates who apply pending results of their qualifying examinations their selection shall be subject to production of proof of their passing the qualifying examination in one attempt or compartmentally at the time of interview for admission.

2. Admissions are made based on the merit rank obtained in the AP POLYCET and the reservations rules stipulated by the government of Andhra Pradesh from time to time.

ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT

The First Year Department provides the foundational academic platform for all incoming undergraduate students across engineering disciplines. It focuses on building core knowledge, engineering aptitude, analytical skills, and professional ethics that are essential for success in specialized engineering streams.

The Department serves as the foundational academic unit responsible for imparting core scientific, mathematical, and engineering principles to all newly admitted undergraduate engineering students.
The department bridges school-level education and professional engineering studies by nurturing analytical thinking, technical skills, and ethical values.

MASTER OF COMPUTER APPLICATIONS Learning modern programming language Designed to meet the shortage of qualified professionals Reduced time for data-heavy tasks Meant to develop better and faster applications.

JOIN WITH US

ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT

  • MCA is a Post Graduate program of three years course spanning over six semesters,  last semester is exclusively reserved for project work.

    Our MCA department is well equipped with qualified and experienced staff, computer laboratories and Internet facilities.
    Students can make use of these facilities to enrich their working knowledge on computer domain.

    Students are admitted into MCA course through ICET entrance examination conducted by government of Andhra Pradesh.

    Students who have passed the Bachelor Degree examination with not less than 50% of the marks in the aggregate with mathematics as one of the subjects at 10+2 level can write the entrance examination.

JOIN WITH US

ABOUT HEAD OF THE DEPARTMENT

Dr Hari Kishan Chapala has received Ph.D in Computer Science and Engineering in 2013 from Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. He is working as Professor and Head in Master of Computer Applications. He has a total of 23 years of experience in Teaching and Administration.He is ratified by JNTUK, Kakinada in 2016. He has authored and published more than 10 research papers in reputed journals. He is nominated as Q-Leader by APSCHE. He is a peer reviewer and Editorial Board member for several Journals.

VISION

    • To emerge as a premier knowledge center for imparting computing education and inculcating human values to solve global challenges

MISSION

  • To enable the students to be knowledgeable and creative through innovative teaching methodologies

    To provide training programs that bridges the gap between academia and industry to produce competitive software professionals

    To inculcate ethical values in students enabling them to become socially committed professionalsTo enhance the research quality and productivity by providing required facilities and industry collaboration

  • PROGRAM EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES (PEOs):
  • PROGRAM SPECIFIC OUTCOMES (PSOs)
  • PROGRAM OUTCOMES (POs)
  • BOS
  • PEO-I: Learn and apply computing and managerial principles to excel in professional career and in the field of Computer Applications as an individual, as part of a team, as an entrepreneur and equip them with orientation towards research.

    PEO-II: Analyze real world problems, design and develop solutions through the knowledge of mathematics and computing principles that are socially acceptable.

    PEO-III: Exhibit professional ethics, cyber regulations and communication skills, engage in lifelong learning and to adapt emerging technologies and tools.

PSO1

Acquire knowledge to face competitive examinations like GATE, GRE and TOFEL etc.

PSO2

Ability to analyze design and model various electrical components, machines & equipment.

PSO3 

Take up challenges in the profession in the fields of power generation, transmission, distribution, equipment design and related fields.

PSO4

Ability to solve economical & social problems maintaining the balance between professional and ethical responsibility.

  • MCA Graduates will be able to: 

    PO1.Computational Knowledge:  Apply knowledge of computing fundamentals, computing specialisation, mathematics, and domain knowledge appropriate for the computing specialisation to the abstraction and conceptualisation of computing models from defined problems and requirements.  

    PO2.Problem Analysis:  Identify, formulate, research literature, and solve complex computing problems reaching substantiated conclusions using fundamental principles of mathematics, computing sciences, and relevant domain disciplines.  

    PO3. Design/development of solutions: Design and evaluate solutions for complex computing problems, and design and evaluate systems, components, or processes that meet specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.  

    PO4.Conduct investigations of complex problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions. 

    PO5. Modern tool usage: Create, select, adapt and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern computing tools to complex computing activities, with an understanding of the limitations. 

    PO6. Professional Ethics:  Understand and commit to professional ethics and cyber regulations, responsibilities, and norms of professional computing practices.  

    PO7. Life-long Learning:   Recognise the need, and have the ability, to engage in independent learning for continual development as a computing professional.  

    PO8. Project management and finance:  Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the computing and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.  

    PO9. Communication Efficacy:  Communicate effectively with the computing community, and with society at large, about complex computing activities by being able to comprehend and write effective reports, design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and understand clear instructions.  

    PO10. Societal and Environmental Concern:   Understand and assess societal, environmental, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues within local and global contexts, and the consequential responsibilities relevant to professional computing practices.  

    PO11. Individual and Team Work:  Function effectively as an individual and as a member or leader in diverse teams and in multidisciplinary environments.  

    PO12. Innovation and Entrepreneurship:  Identify a timely opportunity and using innovation to pursue that opportunity to create value and wealth for the betterment of the individual and society at large.

HOD's Desk

 Dr. Ramanadhula Emmanuel,

Ph.D.; MBA; M.Phil.;

Professor & HOD- Department of MBA.

Over View

The Department of Business Administration is Incorporated in St.ANN’s college of Engineering and Technology in the year of 2006 with an intake of 60 students. The MBA Department at SACET campus is renowned for its pioneering ideas and efforts to impart latest knowledge to its students and creating ethical environment in its surroundings. The Department has excellent Infrastructural facilities and is well equipped with full fledged laboratories, audio-visual facilities, Software tools, Excellent Central as well as Departmental Library with good number of National & International Journals, Magazines and 10 Mbps internet facility.

The main objective of the department right from its inception  has been to provide high quality training as well as technical inputs to our students primarily to meet the requirements of Industry, and R&D establishments both in India and abroad.

Message

  • The Department of Business Administration is renowned for its pioneering ideas and efforts to impart latest knowledge to its students and creating professional environment.

               In order to achieve the basic objectives of MBA curriculum focus is on a unique pedagogy which includes experiential and outcome based learning to supplement the curriculum. Our department provides excellent environment to the students to hone up various management skills and has a continuous process of interaction with corporate, industry leaders through workshops, seminars, lectures and other extracurricular events.

               Our goal is to impart value based quality education along with development of positive attitude, skills and abilities through Management Club Activities, Outbound Activities and Business Lab etc., to apply knowledge in order to meet the challenges of future.

               The institution has highly competent, committed and proficient faculty who have associated their personal aims and growth with that of the institution.

To become a center of excellence in the Mechanical Engineering discipline with effective teaching and learning environment to meet the changing and challenging needs of the modern industry and research originations,  motivate students to pursue higher studies, ignite entrepreneurship skills to enhance national wealth.

Mission

  1. To provide quality education in undergraduate and postgraduate programs, leading to careers as Mechanical Engineering professionals in the industry, government, academic and research organizations.
  2. To be the preferred choice of students, faculty and industry.
  3. To impart skills required to analyze, design and manufacture components and systems.
  4. To develop human resources for the benefit of society and industry through the process of continuous learning and innovative skills in Mechanical Engineering.

     To Develop Competent Management Professionals with strong Ethical Values Capable of Assuming a significant role in Corporate and Society

MECHANICAL ENGINEERING One of the broadest engineering disciplines Study of objects and systems in motion

KNOW MORE

ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, Chirala was rooted in the year 2004 with an initial intake of 60 with the approval of AICTE. With in a short period of time, the department has taken the concrete shape in carrying out the academic and co-curricular activities in an effective way. The Intake was enhanced to 120 in the academic year 2011-12. The department was accredited by NBA, AICTE, New Delhi in the year 2009 and second time in the year 2012, accredited by Institute of Engineers I E (I),Kolkata

KNOW MORE

ABOUT HEAD OF THE DEPARTMENT

  • The department of MECHANICAL ENGINEERING has surpassed many milestones under the able and dynamic leadership of its HOD DR.CH.LAKSHMI TULASI.

KNOW MORE

Dr.Ch.LAKSHMI TULASI

M.Tech, Ph.D
Professor & HOD- Department of ME.

VISION

To become a center of excellence in the Mechanical Engineering discipline with effective teaching and learning environment to meet the changing and challenging needs of the modern industry and research originations,  motivate students to pursue higher studies, ignite entrepreneurship skills to enhance national wealth.

MISSION

  • To provide quality education in undergraduate and postgraduate programs, leading to careers as Mechanical Engineering professionals in the industry, government, academic and research organizations.
  • To be the preferred choice of students, faculty and industry.
  • To impart skills required to analyze, design and manufacture components and systems.
  • To develop human resources for the benefit of society and industry through the process of continuous learning and innovative skills in Mechanical Engineering.

PEO

 

 

DESCRIPTION

 

I

To acquire academic excellence with good leadership qualities, ethical codes and aptitude for life-long learning needed for a successful professional career.

II

To imbibe the necessary attributes for attaining senior Mechanical Engineering positions.

III

To actively engaged in societal Mechanical Engineering activities such as design and safety, energy optimization & economical agricultural production machinery.

IV

To Attain professional certifications and growth in the allied streams of Mechanical Engineering.

V

To Work in research and development organizations to enhance national wealth and security.

Engineering Graduates will be able to:

PO1.   Engineering knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2.    Problem analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3.    Design/development of solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and   design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental   considerations.

PO4.    Conduct investigations of complex problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of  the information to provide valid conclusions.

PO5.    Modern tool usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern   engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

PO6.    The engineer and society: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

PO7.    Environment and sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need     for sustainable development.

PO8.   Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

PO9.    Individual and team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

PO10. Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the  engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.

PO11. Project management and finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

PO12. Life-long learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change

Programme specific outcomes

1.Apply their knowledge in  in the domain of engineering mechanics, thermal and fluid sciences to solve engineering problems utilizing advanced technology.

2. Effectively apply the principles of design, analysis and implementation of mechanical systems/processes which have been learned as a part of the curriculum.

3. Develop and execute new ideas on product design and development with the help of modern CAD/CAM tools, while ensuring best manufacturing practices.

4. Ability to discover, articulate the local industrial problems and solve with the use of Mechanical Engineering tools for realistic outcomes.

Innovations by the Faculty in Teaching and Learning:

The faculty of the department uses various latest pedagogical methods for the enhancement of learning process by the students.


  • Faculty using physical models and 3D models at the time of teaching Drawing class
  • Faculty using models of different Mechanisms at the time of teaching Kinematics of machinery subject.

  • Smart Class room facilities are used by the faculty for showing Animations and Video Lectures.
  • Mode of teaching in this institute is not only limited to the traditional Chalk & Talk methods, but also by the modern technology (e.g.powerpoint presentation, audiovisual teaching etc.) with the traditional one. Faculty shares the study materials among the students via e-mail, websites, hand-outs etc.
  • There is a digital library facility in the campus and the students are encouraged to refer to journals and conference proceedings for their project works and seminars in the latest topics. The library also possesses a number of magazines and periodicals also related to different branches of science and technology which the students may readily access
  • Students are encouraged to visit NPTEL lectures, browse different internet sites to increase their knowledge base about the subject. Moreover, through these activities’ students acquire relevant knowledge which is beyond the syllabus as per the university curriculum
  • Code Tantra is an online learning platform primarily focused on learning coding skills, utilizing an interactive and automated approach to help students learn programming languages like Java, Python, C, HTML, and more through a "learn by doing" methodology. To effective utilization of the facility, separate three hours added in time table and all accessories are provided to the students.

ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT

The department of Civil Engineering was established in the year 2011 with an intake of 60. Eight batches of students nearly 480 have successfully completed their graduation so far from the department. Our strength is our faculty. Tech) programme with initial intake of 24 students with Transportation Engineering as specialization.

The department has nine physical laboratories to fulfill the needs of academic and industrial requirements including are Concrete, Transportation Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering , Environmental Engineering , Survey , Geology , Hydraulic Engineering , Computer aided engineering , GIS & CAD lab, Strength of materials, FM & HM Lab and Irrigation Design and Drawing. All laboratories are equipped with state of the art equipment to suit the emerging technologies and career opportunities

Kiran Kumar has been working as Professor, Department of Civil Engineering in a reputed institution – St. Anns College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala, Bapatla Dist., A.P. since July 2024.  He has put in 25 years of teaching experience in various positions as a Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor.  His areas of Subjects are Water Resources Engineering, Irrigation & Hydraulic Structures, Fluid Mechanics, Hydrology, Design & Drawing of Irrigation Structure etc.  He obtained his B.Tech. from S.V. Education Awards.  He published a book entitled “Integrated Watershed Management in Drought Prone Areas” in the year 2023.

About the Department

Department Overview

The Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering (ECE) was established in the year 2001 with an initial intake of 60 students. Over the years, the department has grown significantly in terms of academic strength, infrastructure, student intake and technical capabilities. At present, the department has an annual intake of 240 students, reflecting its growing demand and contribution to technical education.

The department is supported by a team of well-qualified and experienced faculty members who are committed to providing quality education, practical exposure and professional guidance to students. A majority of the faculty members are ratified by JNTUK, Kakinada, strengthening the academic standards and quality of teaching in the department.

Vision & Mission

Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering

👁️

VISION

Our vision for excellence and innovation

To produce globally competitive engineering graduates through high quality education, to instill high standards of ethics and professionalism and to bring out quality research in the frontier areas of Electronics & Communication Engineering.

🎯

MISSION

Our commitment towards education, research and society

M1

To impart high quality technical education to all students.

M2

To become active life-long learners with the necessary skills, competencies, and ethical values.

M3

To develop human power with creativity, innovation and research.

M4

To inculcate value-based, socially committed professionalism to the cause of overall development of students and society.

Electronics & Communication Engineering  |  Vision • Mission

PEOs, PSOs,POs
PEOs

Program Educational Objectives

The Program Educational Objectives define the professional capabilities expected from graduates of the program.

PEO-I

Fundamental Engineering Knowledge

To acquire fundamental knowledge in basic and applied engineering sciences to formulate and solve problems related to Electronics & Communication Engineering.

PEO-II

Design, Innovation & Solutions

To develop theoretical and practical knowledge in Electronics & Communication Engineering courses to design/innovate and create novel products/solutions to real life problems.

PEO-III

Professionalism & Leadership

To exhibit professionalism, multidisciplinary approach and ethical attitude with good managerial and entrepreneur skills to meet the needs of industry and society.

PEO-IV

Research & Lifelong Learning

To recognize the need for research, further studies and continuous learning to adopt oneself in the ever growing technological scenario.

PSOs

Program Specific Outcomes

Graduates of Electronics & Communication Engineering will be able to:

PSO1

Demonstrate the ability to take up challenges and develop innovative solutions in VLSI design, Embedded systems, IoT and related industrial applications using modern tools.

PSO2

Acquire strong competency in wireless communications, Antennas and Computer vision enabling effective participation in advanced research and technological development.

PSO3

Apply engineering knowledge with ethical responsibility and leadership skills to design solutions that address technological and societal problems.

POs

Program Outcomes

Graduates of the program will demonstrate the following professional outcomes.

PO1

Engineering Knowledge

Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2

Problem Analysis

Identify, formulate, review research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions with consideration for sustainable development. (WK1 to WK4)

PO3

Design/Development of Solutions

Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design/develop systems/components/processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, culture, society and environment as required. (WK5)

PO4

Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems

Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modelling, analysis & interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8)

PO5

Engineering Tool Usage

Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering & IT tools, including prediction and modelling recognizing their limitations to solve complex engineering problems. (WK2 and WK6)

PO6

The Engineer and The World

Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7)

PO7

Ethics

Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclusion; adhere to national & international laws. (WK9)

PO8

Individual and Collaborative Team Work

Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse/multi-disciplinary teams.

PO9

Communication

Communicate effectively and inclusively within the engineering community and society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences.

PO10

Project Management and Finance

Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

PO11

Life-Long Learning

Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for:

  • Independent and life-long learning.
  • Adaptability to new and emerging technologies.
  • Critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change. (WK8)

ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT

The Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering was established in the year 2001 with an intake of 60 students and the current intake of the department is 240. The department has well qualified and experienced faculty members and majority of the faculty members are ratified by the JNTUK, Kakinada University. The department has state-of-the-art laboratory equipment like GPS trainer, Satellite trainer, Antenna trainer, RFID system etc. to enrich the students in the field of Electronics & Commination Engineering. The department received three IRNSS receivers from ISRO to explore more on Indian navigation system. The department also offers M.Tech. Program with Embedded systems (ES) specialization with an intake of 24.

ABOUT HEAD OF THE DEPARTMENT

Dr.D.Rajendra Prasad has received Ph.D in Electronics & Communication Engineering in 2017 from JNTUK Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh. He has a total of 24 years of experience in Teaching and Administration He is currently working as Professor and Head, department of ECE in St.Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology (Autonomus), Chirala, Andhra Pradesh, India. He is ratified by JNTUK, Kakinada in 2010. He has published his work in 43 refereed International journals and International conference proceedings. He is an active reviewer for various reputed journals like IEEE access, IEEE systems journal, IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics, International journal of communication systems etc,. His Research areas include Wireless Communications, Wireless sensor Networks, Antennas & Internet of Things. He is a (Fellow) member of various professional bodies like FIETE, IAENG, SDIWC, IE, and ISTE.
